title: Introduction to netkit
text: common starting point list nodes — differentially expressed genes, known disease genes, set drug targets — question relate one another. extract_subnetwork() answers five strategies increasing ambition. "induced" keeps seeds whatever edges run : usually almost nothing, baseline others compared . "neighbors" adds surrounding neighborhood, max_degree available exclude promiscuous hubs — without cap, first-neighbor expansion hub-dominated network returns network.  "shortest_paths" takes union every shortest path every pair seeds — classic “connect gene list”. "steiner" instead finds approximate minimum Steiner tree: smallest tree connects , via Kou–Markowsky–Berman heuristic. union keeps every equally short route grows quickly; tree keeps one connecting structure far easier read, usually makes better figure.  "diffusion" reuses diffusion machinery next section, keeping top-scoring vertices instead: Unlike netkit, return plot element: like plot_Net(), find_modules() highlight_nodes(), render base graphics plot object hand back.

title: Weighted networks: strength or distance?
text: weight can mean one two opposite things. strength means larger values bind endpoints tightly. BioGRID confidence score 0.9 stronger claim 0.2. co-expression correlation 0.95 closer relationship 0.3. distance means larger values push endpoints apart. reaction time, transit cost, dissimilarity. one changes answer almost every network question, opposite directions. igraph — netkit built — reads weight edge attribute implicitly, giving different meanings different functions: cost betweenness(), distances(), diameter() mean_distance(), strength cluster_louvain() community detection algorithms. looks like. graph barbell: two cliques joined single bridge. Read strength, bridge reliable edge graph, crossing cheap. Read cost, expensive edge, crossing dominate path uses . Comparing two readings’ path lengths directly meaningless — one measured units confidence units 1/confidence. comparable share crossing path bridge accounts : Read strength, bridge cheapest hop route accounts 5% . Read cost, number makes expensive hop, accounting 80%. way get right inspection — sets numbers look perfectly plausible.
code: g <- disjoint_union(make_full_graph(4), make_full_graph(4)) V(g)$name <- c(paste0("L", 1:4), paste0("R", 1:4)) g <- add_edges(g, c("L1", "R1"))  # A confidence score: the bridge is a very well-supported interaction, the # within-clique edges less so. E(g)$confidence <- 0.1 E(g)$confidence[E(g)["L1" %--% "R1"]] <- 1.0 bridge_share <- function(type) {   w <- as_netkit_weights_demo(g, "confidence", type)   # Cost of getting from one clique to the other, and the bridge's own cost.   total <- distances(g, v = "L2", to = "R2", weights = w$distance)[1, 1]   bridge <- w$distance[as.numeric(E(g)["L1" %--% "R1"])]   c(path_cost = total, bridge_cost = bridge, bridge_share = bridge / total) }  rbind(strength = bridge_share("strength"),       distance = bridge_share("distance")) #>          path_cost bridge_cost bridge_share #> strength      21.0           1   0.04761905 #> distance       1.2           1   0.83333333

Extracts interpretable subnetworks around set nodes, including approximate Steiner trees Kou, Markowsky Berman (1981) doi:10.1007/BF00288961 . Propagates influence seed nodes using Laplacian smoothing, heat-kernel random-walk--restart diffusion, degree-matched permutation nulls, simulates network robustness progressive node removal. Observed metrics can tested degree-preserving random ensembles. Edge weights supported throughout, explicit declaration whether weight means strength distance. Matrix operations use sparse representations throughout methods remain usable large graphs.
